local_facts.claim: Austin Watershed Protection's FloodPro shows floodplain maps, storm-drain systems, models, and elevation certificates; the city says about 10% of Austin land lies in floodplain.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A restoration visit must separate outdoor flooding and drainage exposure from an internal plumbing failure, then document the source and affected areas before drying decisions are made.
local_facts.title: Floodplain and storm-drain information is address-specific

local_facts.claim: During Austin's October 31, 2013 Halloween Flood, Onion Creek at US 183 reached a record 41 feet and rose 11 feet in 15 minutes; 659 homes in the Onion Creek neighborhood were damaged.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Flash-flood water can arrive and spread fast, so outdoor water is treated as potentially contaminated and removal, cleaning, containment, and drying begin as soon as access is safe.
local_facts.title: Onion Creek rose 11 feet in 15 minutes in 2013

local_facts.claim: Austin Watershed Protection reports more than 9,000 buildings in the city's 100-year floodplain and more than 300 bridges subject to flooding.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Creek and floodplain exposure is a local reality. A clear record of where water entered helps distinguish flood damage from a burst pipe and guides safe restoration scope.
local_facts.title: Creek-flood exposure is part of Austin restoration planning

anchors.label: Water categories under the industry standard
anchors.detail: The consensus standard is ANSI/IICRC S500, Standard for Professional Water Damage Restoration, fifth edition, 2021. Its Category 3 definition covers grossly contaminated water including sewage, wasteline backflows originating beyond a trap, and rising water from rivers or streams. The standard body also states that wind-driven rain is not automatically Category 3.
anchors.source_name: ANSI/IICRC S500 fifth edition, category position statement

anchors.label: City residential plumbing permit
anchors.detail: The fiscal year 2026 homeowner permitting schedule lists a plumbing permit at $200.43, up from $184.70, and applies the same figure to common residential building permits and small projects. The schedule took effect October 1, 2025.
anchors.source_name: City of Austin homeowner permitting fees, fiscal year 2026

anchors.label: Utility leak bill adjustment window
anchors.detail: Austin Water offers a leak adjustment under City of Austin Code section 15-9-141 and asks for the request within 90 days of repairing the leak, with the paid repair invoice, account number, service address and date range of the high bills.
anchors.source_name: Austin Water high water bill options
